dedupe_keys.name: bundestag research services veroffentlichung von daten zu kritischer infrastruktur kritis im energie und telekommunikationssektor 2026

description: This 57-page report by the German Bundestag's research services reviews which data on electricity, gas and telecommunications infrastructure, such as capacities, routes and technical design, must be public under EU and German law, and whether the legislator could restrict their publication. It was completed on 23 February 2026 after the January 2026 attack on the Berlin power grid and the debate that followed, in which the government, the BDEW and VKU associations and a grid operator argued that published data make attacks easier. It covers network development plans for power, gas and hydrogen, structural and network data under section 23c of the Energy Industry Act, the national information platform, the Marktstammdatenregister, the national transparency platform, the telecommunications Infrastrukturatlas, planning approval procedures and environmental and geodata access rules. Coverage is Germany with its EU law basis. Format and access: a free German-language PDF. Licence: copyright of the Bundestag. Caveats: it is a legal analysis that reflects the state at writing and is not the Bundestag's position. It maps which open infrastructure data may disappear, which matters for resilience and hazard exposure models of German networks. Related catalogue records are the Marktstammdatenregister and SMARD electricity market data.
